summary:
StellarX is an interactive space mission design and management simulation game developed using Python and Streamlit. It allows students and beginners to design virtual space missions by selecting mission objectives, rockets, scientific instruments, orbits, and power systems while managing limited resources and budgets.

The project addresses the challenge of understanding complex aerospace engineering concepts and mission design decisions by transforming theoretical knowledge into an interactive, practical learning experience. It uses NASA engineering resources, including the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook and CubeSat 101, to establish realistic mission constraints.

What makes StellarX unique is its built-in Engineering Advisor, which detects design conflicts, such as budget overruns and power shortages, and provides real-time engineering feedback. Users also receive a mission feasibility score out of 100 and a comprehensive mission report.

StellarX is important because it makes space engineering more accessible, encourages scientific curiosity, and helps future innovators understand the complex decisions involved in designing successful space missions.
details:
How does the project work?

StellarX is an interactive space mission design and management simulation game. Users begin by selecting mission objectives and configuring their spacecraft, including rockets, scientific instruments, orbits, and power systems. The simulation evaluates their choices using engineering equations and realistic constraints. It then provides real-time feedback, identifies design conflicts, and generates a mission feasibility score out of 100 along with a detailed mission report.

What are its benefits?

StellarX makes complex aerospace engineering concepts easier to understand through interactive learning. It allows users to experiment with different mission designs, understand engineering trade-offs, manage limited resources, and learn from design mistakes in a risk-free virtual environment.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space science and engineering more accessible to students and beginners, encourage interest in aerospace fields, and help future innovators develop problem-solving and engineering decision-making skills.

What tools and technologies were used?

We developed the project using Python, Streamlit, NumPy, and Pandas. We also used aerospace engineering trade-off equations and NASA resources, including the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook (SP-2016-6105) and CubeSat 101. The current version is entirely software-based and does not require physical hardware.

What makes the project creative?

The creative aspect of StellarX is its combination of educational gaming and aerospace engineering simulation. Its built-in Engineering Advisor automatically detects conflicts, such as budget overruns and insufficient power, and guides users toward better mission configurations. It transforms complex engineering decisions into an interactive challenge.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered mission objectives, spacecraft mass, power requirements, budget limitations, data rates, orbital parameters, payload capacity, and overall mission feasibility. We also considered educational accessibility, ease of use, and the accuracy of the engineering models.
